entries.title: rustup-init 1.28.2 for AArch64 Linux
claims: The repository bootstrap identifies and verifies the versioned official AArch64 Linux rustup-init artifact.
entries.limitations: Bootstrap input only; it does not freeze the P003 host/target toolchain or prove the AArch64 bootstrap run.

entries.title: rustup-init 1.28.2 for x86_64 Linux
claims: The repository bootstrap identifies and verifies the versioned official x86_64 Linux rustup-init artifact.
entries.limitations: Bootstrap input only; it does not freeze the P003 host/target toolchain.

entries.title: just 1.42.4 crate archive
claims: The bootstrap installs the recorded just release using its published locked Cargo graph.
entries.limitations: Candidate developer tool only; its transitive sources are not yet a sealed offline mirror.

entries.title: Erlang/OTP 29.0.5 source release
claims: The frozen runtime candidate uses the immutable OTP 29.0.5 source release.
entries.limitations: The release identity does not by itself establish compatibility with Elixir; the offline runtime-pair smoke supplies that evidence.

entries.title: Elixir 1.20.4 immutable source archive
claims: The frozen runtime candidate builds Elixir 1.20.4 from an immutable commit archive.
entries.limitations: The source identity does not prove the selected OTP pair runs; the network-disabled Mix smoke supplies that evidence.

entries.title: Elixir 1.20 compatibility with Erlang/OTP
entries.limitations: Documentation establishes the supported range; the repository smoke tests only the selected OTP 29.0.5 pair.

entries.title: Rust 1.89.0 dated channel manifest
claims: The dated official manifest identifies Rust/Cargo 1.89.0 host and AArch64 target component artifacts.
entries.limitations: The manifest pins compiler components but does not validate the later kernel or userspace outputs.

entries.title: LLVM 20.1.8 source release
claims: LLVM/Clang/LLD 20.1.8 is the frozen C, freestanding C++, and linker candidate.
entries.limitations: P003 pins source and native host archives; later tasks own executable AArch64 compiler and linker probes.

entries.title: musl 1.2.5 source release
claims: musl 1.2.5 is the frozen static AArch64 userspace C library source.
entries.limitations: This pin does not claim a completed sysroot; RB-T-P005 owns the target build and executable probes.

entries.title: QEMU 11.1.0 source release
claims: QEMU 11.1.0 is the frozen emulator candidate behind the versioned virt-11.1 runner profiles.
entries.limitations: RB-T-P014 still owns executable validation and the final machine, CPU, GIC, HWCAP, and DTB contract.

entries.title: Meson 1.9.0 source release
claims: Meson 1.9.0 is the frozen host build-utility candidate.
entries.limitations: The pin records source closure; later build tasks own use of Meson in target-producing commands.

entries.title: Ninja 1.13.1 Linux release
claims: Ninja 1.13.1 is the frozen Linux build-utility candidate; the source lock separately pins both Linux host architectures.
entries.limitations: This ledger entry identifies the x86_64 artifact; the AArch64 artifact has its own digest in the sealed source lock.

entries.title: Python 3.13.7 Bookworm multi-architecture OCI image
claims: The clean Linux builder uses this immutable OCI index with separately pinned x86_64 and AArch64 child manifests.
entries.limitations: The aggregate image contains distribution packages with component-specific licenses; the receipt records observed tools but does not claim bit-reproducible builds.

entries.title: Tyn Rust kernel and BEAM host prior art
claims: At the pinned commit Tyn contains an x86_64 Rust kernel, a static musl OTP 27.3.4.2 ERTS artifact, a narrow Linux syscall personality, and a conservative init-time futex spin-yield valve coupled to the serial_shell ready marker.

Tyn is feasibility and warning evidence only; its self-reported KVM, Nitro, TCG, reliability, networking, and TLS observations do not prove this project's AArch64 QEMU virt, TCG, KVM, or HVF behavior.
entries.limitations: Source and committed artifacts were independently inspected and the kernel rebuilt, but this orb had no /dev/kvm or qemu-system-x86_64, so no Tyn boot or reported run-rate claim was reproduced.
